evidence: statusFor() maps ValidationError/BadRequestError/parse errors to 400, NotFoundError to 404, ConflictError to 409 and anything else to 500. This turns errors into HTTP status codes, which is transport (infrastructure) work.
isJsonParseError() checks the Express body-parser 'entity.parse.failed' type, which is framework-specific logic suited to infrastructure.
errorHandler (ErrorRequestHandler) calls res.status().json(...) and console.error, which is HTTP response writing and logging, both infrastructure concerns.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file is Express error-handling middleware in the infrastructure layer. Everything it does is transport work. It maps domain and request error types to HTTP status codes, recognises Express body-parser JSON parse errors, logs unexpected errors, and writes JSON error responses. That is the job of an infrastructure HTTP adapter. It contains no business rules, invariants or domain decisions. It only translates already-classified errors into HTTP semantics, and that translation belongs at the transport boundary.
